result.unmet_or_deviations:
1. 'Training-relevant state' for state_u01200.pt: I compare the whole file (agent incl. actor/critic/opponent/frozen/both Adam states/minibatch rng/refresh count/conc scales, the four numpy rng streams, torch_generator_state, counters, snapshot_log, schedule_positions, flags, seed namespaces, phase bookkeeping) EXCEPT the three process-global RNG states (torch_global_rng_state, numpy_global_rng_state, python_random_state). cr1_compare/v1.1 exclude exactly those, so I followed that relation; they are compared and reported as the informational field state.global_rng_identical (it was True for parents_A vs itself) but are NOT required. If the owner wants them required, it is a one-line change in compare_states. No wall-clock fields exist in the state file (V1.strip is applied anyway).
2. An export present in the arm run but absent from parents_A at an update <= bound counts as a failure (set equality inside the bound, as cr1_compare._weights_diff does), not only missing ones.
3. C4 requires status.json state == 'done', exit_code == 0 and final_global_update == 1600 (the end of Phase A); the spec only said 'finished OK'. It does not read final_v2.json (refine_analysis.classify_run does; I did not import it because it pulls in the whole analysis stack).
4. C5 for A_peak35/A_peak40 is descriptive only: first differing export, ok always True, shown as '--' in the table and excluded from the C5 count (summary C5 n = 40 for the default run; a missing run directory still fails every check including C5 of those arms). The v2_updates.csv row comparison (all non-wall-clock columns, as text, on the common columns) is done for the two late arms only (rows <= bound); for A_peak35/40 it would be meaningless, so I did not compute it for them.
5. For the late arms 'sanity' is required and means: some export beyond the bound differs (first_diff_update not None); the first-differing-export > bound part is then implied by the prefix check. The check does not require that the first differing export is exactly bound+25.
6. Multiprocessing uses ProcessPoolExecutor with torch.set_num_threads(1) per worker (workers=1 runs inline). The caller must still export OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1.
7. In the wave-A validation I used d581b3c as --code-commit (the commit in the R2b manifests), so C1 compared an empty diff; C1's dirty/commit/path logic is covered by the synthetic tests, not by that real run.
result.oddities_in_existing_code:
- tools/v2/r2b_launch_checks.py never looks at status.json (so a failed run with a good manifest passes it); the R2c tool adds C4 as specified. It also keeps a per-call commit cache dict where I used lru_cache; both split git's output with str.split(), which would break on file names containing spaces (copied the same behaviour; not an issue in this repo).
- launch_refine.r2b_comparator_config is documented for 'an R2b wave' but also handles R2c via the R2C_EXPECTED_DIFFS membership test; the docstring does not mention R2c (not a bug).
- tests/test_v2_r2c.py already exists untracked (another task's file); my tests are in tests/test_v2_r2c_tools.py to avoid clashing. git status also shows modified (not by me) run/run_v2_stagewise.py, tools/v2/launch_refine.py, tests/test_v2_r2b.py, tests/test_v2_r2b_gaps.py and an untracked reports/v2/refine_r2c/.
- R1's parents_A run_config.json files have no R2b keys while the R2b/R2c manifests' input_config do (the tools add the defaults before diffing, as the R2b tool does); the launcher's build for r2c_waveS matches the on-disk R1 config in everything except start_weights (verified on q50 seed10501 for the four arms).
- A real-data fact worth knowing for the verification of D2: R2b's A_censored first differing export agrees with d1_first_flagged_update in all 18 runs that have a flag (diff export = first multiple of 25 at or after the flagged update), which supports the 'bit-identical before the first clamped draw' reading used in the tests; two runs (q50 seed10502, q60 seed10506) never flag and never differ over all 64 exports."

result.unmet_or_deviations: Nothing in the spec is unmet. Choices and additions: (1) A full tie of the first two eligible arms on all four key components gives selected null, outcome unresolved_tie, with the reason stated; arm name is never used to decide, only to order the ranking deterministically. (2) Exit code 3 when any arm is incomplete; a complete run with no arm selected exits 0. (3) Complete means all 20 planned runs done and all 10 paired differences per q finite; eligible means complete and (a) met at both q and b_status equal to holds, so a pending (b) is not eligible. (4) The R2b reference arms are named R2b_A_peak25 and R2b_A_peak50 in tables (avoids a clash with same-named main arms in validation mode) and carry the label R2b reference (descriptive, not eligible), so R1 criterion_table gives them no criterion row and they never enter select_arm. (5) The boot seed is recorded as boot_seed and n_boot columns in paired.csv, criterion.csv, selection_inputs.csv, ranking.csv and the displayed primary and criterion CSVs, plus analysis_info.json, selection.json and both reports; non-bootstrap CSVs do not carry it. The verbatim rule text in 03_selection.md says 20261005, and the seed actually used is printed right below; in validation mode they differ and both are shown. (6) --r2b-root defaults to the R2b worktree path and is skipped with a note if the path does not exist, or is empty or none; not given cannot be detected because the default exists. (7) Peak-set visitation share is the R2b tool value, cumulative over the whole phase, so for late arms it mixes bin-balanced and peak-focused updates (stated in the report). (8) Figures: 4 per-arm paired-dot figures plus 1 overview figure (png and pdf). The pilot report has no RNG-divergence, dispersion or logged-trajectory tables since the task did not list them. (9) The module saves R.BOOT_SEED before importing the R2b module and restores it afterwards, undoing the R2b import-time side effect so other test modules in one pytest process are not affected; compute sets the CLI seed before any statistic.

result.oddities_in_existing_code: Found, not fixed; no existing file was touched. (a) tools/v2/refine_r2b_analysis.py line 40 sets R.BOOT_SEED = 20261004 at import; any other importer in the same process inherits it while R1 tests expect 20261003 (effect depends on collection order, since tests/test_v2_refine_analysis.py loads its own module copy under the same sys.modules name). R2c saves and restores the value around the import. (b) R.paired_tables returns a seed-level DataFrame with no columns at all when no arm run is complete, so B.arm_figures (R2b line 745) raises AttributeError on seed_level.arm; the R2b tool cannot write its reports for a wave with no complete run. R2c reindexes the seed-level table to fixed columns. (c) The R2b pre-registration section 6 and Addendum 2 say a missing reference file stops the analysis, but R.extract_wave only records a parent_u1600 row with an anomaly text, and missing runs become missing rows. (d) R.paired_tables stores n_better as float with NaN for undirected metrics, so paired.csv shows 6.0 and empty cells; R.cost_table tests if r[mean_phase_local_updates], truthy for NaN, and only works because NaN/NaN does not raise. (e) R.fig_paired_dots emits No artists with labels UserWarnings for empty arms. (f) R.completeness_table looks up set-aside originals by (arm, q) from a 4-component path, so it finds nothing for the 3-component R1 parents_A baseline and for prefixed reference names; R2c shows n/a there. (g) B.arm_notable has an A_censored branch that is dead for R2c; B.run_extras hard-codes the pathwise arm sets (harmless here). (h) The merge in B.extract makes rng_div columns float when no never string is present; the CSV text is unchanged but a default pandas read shows 8.0 instead of 8. Note on environment: a hook refused compound bash commands that mention another worktree, so other worktrees files were read via scratchpad scripts and absolute paths.
